children: Berkshire Hathaway bought more Delta Air Lines shares and sold some of its Bank of America stock in the third quarter, reshaping its portfolio as fuel costs and rising interest rates squeezed two of its largest holdings.

The Omaha-based conglomerate, which is currently by chief executive Greg Abel, raised its Delta stake by 12% by buying 7.13 million shares. That position was worth $5.37 billion at the end of the quarter.

The changes marked a portfolio revision under Abel, who succeeded Warren Buffett aged 96, at the start of this year. Reuters reported on Monday that Buffett still controlled roughly 13% of Berkshire's common stock, after he donated $5.5 billion to nonprofit foundations.

Buffett had announced in July that he planned to sell his large stake in Berkshire Hathaway over the next eight years. He also said he would stop making donations to the Gates Foundation, run by his longtime friend Bill Gates.
That decision had been made after the US Justice Department released a large collection of documents that renewed scrutiny of Gates' ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

Berkshire added to Delta as the Atlanta-based airline's shares tumbled 11% in the third quarter. The war between the United States and Iran pushed up jet fuel prices, which hurt the whole airline industry. It was the stock's worst quarterly performance since the first quarter of 2025, when it plunged 28%. Delta also cut its full-year earnings forecast last month, citing a surge in fuel costs.
The bet has paid off so far as Delta shares rose 3.8% in the fourth quarter to date, while the S&P 500 fell 3.1%, and the airline's stock gained nearly 15% over the past month.

Berkshire moved in the opposite direction on Bank of America, trimming its holding by nearly 6% and selling more than $1.6 billion worth of stock. The bank's shares fell more than 4% in the third quarter as interest rates surged, inflation stayed stubbornly high and investors expected tighter Federal Reserve policy.
In September, the 30-year US Treasury yield rose above 5.6%, its highest level since 2002.

Despite the share sale, Bank of America remained one of Berkshire Hathaway's top holdings, with the stake valued at $24.8 billion at the end of the third quarter. Berkshire also started a new position in Bending Spoons and nearly doubled its stake in homebuilder Lennar during the same quarter.

title: Berkshire Hathaway adds to Delta, trims Bank of America in third quarter portfolio shake-up
